content:
maria: Heads-up — after flipping on the stricter validator for structured fncalls last night, we’ve seen a 6% spike in rejects for the `pdf-extract` tool and a handful of customer requests hitting fallback routing but not getting routed. iirc fallback should route to `extract-lite` automatically.

kai: ugh. saw the spike in logs too. are the rejects all schema-type errors (missing fields) or parsing errors?

maria: mostly schema rejects. payloads where `pages` is an int vs array and one with `metadata` as null. examples in infra logs: 

maria: ```
2025-03-11T02:12:03Z WARN invoke.reject schema=fncall pdf-extract request_id=rb-abc123 reason="pages: expected array, got int" route=primary
2025-03-11T02:12:05Z WARN fallback.decision request_id=rb-abc123 candidate=extract-lite decision=NO_MATCH reason="tool-signature-mismatch"
```

ash: interesting — fallback decision = NO_MATCH means the routing predicate thinks `extract-lite` can’t handle that signature. but extract-lite should accept the more permissive shape. did the handshake metadata change?

kai: telemetry shows route_binding for pdf-extract is strict-canary and extract-lite has `accepts_variants=false` in the model-catalog entry. when can we change that?

maria: product-ux mapped that flag to reduce accidental silent fallbacks for legacy users. but the intended behavior for schema upgrades was: validator rejects -> scorer attempts permissive coercion -> fallback if coercion succeeds. looks like coercion step is skipped for strict-canary.

sre-oncall: impact? are customers seeing errors or silent quality regressions? any billing noise?

maria: some customers get immediate fncall error responses (400-ish) where they used to get a downgraded run on extract-lite. billing: token counts down but tool call failed so we’re not marking success; ops says a few large accounts got throttled retries, increasing error rates and support tickets.

dev-bot: deploy 2025-03-11T00:00 -> validator-service:v2.1 rolled to 10% hosts in eu-west at 00:05 (traffic slice id: vs-canary-10). No automated rollback triggered.

ash: root cause hypothesis: validator v2.1 intentionally tightened the handshake match to avoid coercion. fallback logic relies on a separate acceptance flag (`accepts_variants`). we accidentally set `accepts_variants=false` for extract-lite in the model-catalog migration earlier this month. two ways to fix: 1) flip accepts_variants to true for extract-lite (fast revert), or 2) add coercion step inside validator for strict-canary before rejecting (safer long term).

kai: preference: quick revert to restore customer UX, then schedule validator coercion work. but need dashboard/alerts to distinguish strict-canary rejects from expected rejects. right now alerts fire the same.

product-ux: +1 for revert. also we should show a distinct telemetry tag `validation_mode=canary|strict|permissive` in the console to explain why a call took a fallback or failed. customers keep asking why the same prompt sometimes fails.

maria: agreed. operational plan: 
- flip `accepts_variants=true` for extract-lite in model-catalog (ops change) 
- patch dashboard: add `validation_mode` in per-route trace and a small note in the route list UI (product) 
- ticket for validator: add permissive coercion step for fncall flows and feature flag to enable in canary 
- add sampling telemetry to capture example payloads for rejects (PII-stripped)

ash: i can do the catalog flip now. will also add a deprecation tag to the catalog entry so we can revert if needed.

sre-oncall: please also mute the existing alert for schema.rejects.rate until we have the split; otherwise paging noise will keep going. can we set alert to fire only if rejects increase >150% AND `validation_mode!=canary`?

maria: good call. i’ll open the alert change PR.

kai: timeline? if ops flips now we should see reject rate drop in ~2m and fallbacks resume. product to track customer messages and update runbook.

ash: flipped accepts_variants=true for extract-lite; new config published to catalog-service, version 2025-03-11T02:20.

dev-bot: catalog-service publish success: id=mc-789, version=2025-03-11T02:20

maria: monitoring: rejects down to baseline and fallback decisions now showing candidate=extract-lite decision=OK.

product-ux: will add `validation_mode` label in next console patch. filing UX ticket now (PX-5241).

kai: follow-ups: 1) add `validation_mode` to telemetry and traces, 2) make alerting aware of canary context, 3) long-term: add coercion step to validator v2.2.

maria: thanks team. I’ll update the support thread and the rollback notes. :thumbsup:
